claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to maintain a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide above 900 °C is governed by a reactive-element effect associated with X.
Al forms strong, adherent oxides such as alumina.
Al promotes formation of a continuous oxide layer with a low growth rate.
The Al-promoted oxide scale better matches the substrate in thermal expansion and mechanical compliance.
Improved thermal-expansion matching and mechanical compliance reduce oxide-scale stresses.
Reduced oxide-scale stress suppresses cracking and spallation.
Oxides produced when X is Si or Mn are less adherent than the oxide produced when X is Al.
Oxides associated with Si or Mn are more susceptible to stress-driven cracking or spallation.
A continuous alumina-rich sub-layer adheres well to the underlying metallic matrix.
An adherent alumina-rich sub-layer minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch and interfacial stress accumulation.
Reaction of Al with oxygen forms stable, adherent oxide that slows oxidation kinetics.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys will retain a coherent protective oxide above 900 °C with minimal cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn alloys will develop less-adherent, more rapidly growing oxides than the Al-containing alloy under otherwise similar conditions.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn oxide scales will crack or spall more readily than those on the Al-containing alloy.
Significant departures from equilibrium microstructure may alter the predicted oxidation behavior.
Additional environmental variables such as cycling stresses may alter the predicted oxidation behavior.
